newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut t-bill issue raises 311.6 bln pounds.
newsitem.headline: Beirut t-bill issue raises 311.6 bln pounds.

text.p: Lebanon's weekly treasury bill issue of February 27 raised 311.6 billion Lebanese pounds after the Bank of Lebanon restricted sales of most bills.
The previous issue raised 322.5.6 billion pounds.
The issue posted a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 67 billion pounds. It raised the following amounts (in billion of pounds, previous week in brackets):

The central bank said only seven percent of all competitive bids -- those made by Lebanese institutions -- were accepted up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills and seven percent for six-month bills. It was five percent for 12-month and 20 percent for two-year bills.

The Bank also restricted the acceptance of non-competitive bids -- those made by private individuals and foreign investors -- for three- and six-month bills. It approved only seven percent up to the discount rate and yield for three-month bills and also seven percent for six-month bills.
However, all non-competitive bids for 12-month and 24-month bills were accepted, the Bank said.
The Lebanese pound closed at 1,547.75 to the dollar on Monday from 1,548.25 a week earlier and 1,587 a year ago.
